_comment: MERGE FRAGMENTS, and the stories they belong to.
A merge chunk has no front door (docs/foafos-story-layering-20260730.md):
it diverts into knots its host declares and reads variables its host owns,
so it CANNOT compile alone and it is not a work on its own. Checking it as
a standalone story reports a fault that is really the file doing its job.
So fink-check does not skip fragments — it checks them the only way they
are ever run: as the UNION the session compiles. Every path below is
repo-relative. A file listed under `merge` is not checked on its own.
`expect: "collision"` inverts the test: the union MUST fail to compile.
That is the fixture proving two authors who both declare `VAR diamonds`
or both define `=== coin ===` are caught by the real compiler rather than
silently overwriting each other — a refusal the runner turns into a story
